entries.title: Bolzano/Alto Adige in Italian print media and propaganda, 1919–1943: what is digitized, where, and a first article harvest
facts: Notes of 22 October 2026 on the 1919-43 press about Bolzano: what is digitized, where, how to search it, and a harvest of 48 dated Alpenzeitung and Dolomiten items, 31 pinned to a page and downloaded (notes 03, §1)
Teßmann's own site blocked scripts, so all Teßmann content came through Europeana's 2019 copy under the Public Domain Mark; the web-search budget ran out partway (notes 03, method caveats, [V])
La Provincia di Bolzano is not on Teßmann; it is online as a page-image gallery without OCR at the Biblioteca Provinciale Italiana Claudia Augusta, 21.04.1927-27.04.1941 (notes 03, §1, Takeaway, [V])
Search tip: use the Alpenzeitung's German calques: 'halbländlichen' not 'semirurali', 'Volkszug' not 'treno popolare', 'Industriezone' not 'zona industriale' (notes 03, §1B, [V])

Compares the same events in LPB, AZ, Dolomiten and La Stampa (Victory Monument 1928, industrial zone 1935, Option 1939-40): LPB speaks to Italian readers, AZ and DOL to German speakers [I] (notes 03, §1E)
Further sections: the Touring Club's Le Vie d'Italia and the 1936 Giacomelli series, a La Stampa harvest, propaganda volumes, press photography ('Foto Walsa') (notes 03, §2-5)
Tags: [V] verified in the session, [V-img] read off a page image, [U] unopened summary or snippet, [I] inference (notes 03, header)

entries.title: Alto Adige: cenni geografici e statistici
facts: A. R. Toniolo, Alto Adige: cenni geografici e statistici, Novara, Istituto Geografico De Agostini, 1919; scan from the University of Illinois on the Internet Archive (manifest)

Listed among the period books 'presenting the province to Italians' on the Internet Archive; with Borgese 1921 one of the two most relevant, and downloaded because out of copyright (notes 03, §4, [V])
The celebratory municipal and party volumes ('Bolzano fascista', decennial volumes, industrial-zone brochures) were not found online; these two books were (notes 03, §4)

entries.title: Dolomiten, 14 July 1928, page 2
facts: Page 2 (of 12): Dolomiten on the unveiling: 'abroad should finally renounce hostility to the fascist government' (manifest)

entries.title: Alpenzeitung, 29 October 1931, page 3
facts: Page 3 (of 8): 'Eröffnung von Bauwerken des Regimes: Drususbrücke ...' (the 28 Oct. 1931 inaugurations) (manifest); the Europeana OCR is garbled (notes 03, §1C, item 11)

Headline: 'Die Feier des 9. Jahrestages der fascistischen Revolution in Bolzano. Eröffnung von Bauwerken des Regimes: Drususbrücke, städt. Badeanstalt, Palast der Krankenkasse, Rundfunksender der „Eiar", Elektrizitätswerk in Val d'Ega, Artilleriekaserne in Oltrisarco, Tramlinie von Vurza nach Laives usw. - Aushebung der Jungen Italienerinnen' (notes 07, §1, [T])

At 9 a.m. Prefect Marziali was received at the Drususbrücke 'vom Erbauer Ing. Cav. Albini und dem technischen Stab'; a scissor cut, the tricolour ribbon fell and the bridge was handed to traffic (notes 07, §1, [T])

'Werke des Regimes - Die Drususbrücke': 102.30 m long, three arches (middle span 34.70 m), reinforced concrete faced in porphyry; cost 3,000,000 lire, 800,000 of it from the Comune; works began 9 January 1930 (notes 07, §1, [T])

The corner piers carry helmets with a Roman shield and swords that 'mark the beginning and the end of the war'; the columns with the Roman eagles rest on globes carried by the lictor's bundle. The notes read this as settling 'Roman or fascist': both, by design (notes 07, §1, [T])
Doubt: the builder 'Albini' is not among the engineers (Miozzi, Ricci) named by the secondary sources of thread 05; perhaps the site or contractor's engineer [INF] (notes 07, §1)

Seen in the image: the banner headline is set in a condensed bold roman (sans-serif) type and the long subhead in roman, while the body text and the side heading 'Werke des Regimes' are in Fraktur; the five further pictures are hand captures of the same page in the Teßmann viewer (manifest 07)
The _OCR.txt sidecar is Europeana's raw, uncorrected full text of the page; check quotations against the image (manifest)
